To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antifreeze protein III improves the protection of sea bream cryopreserved spermatozoon against freezing-thawing with respect to DMO or DMO plus antifreeze protein I, and that the ability of antifreeze protein to protect sea brem spermatozoon can be, at last in part, ascribe to reducing changes in sperm protein profile occurring in the freezing-thaw procedure.
the antifreeze protein (AFPIII) addition to cryoprotectant medium improves the protection against freezing-thawing with respect to D.M.S.O. or DMSO+AFPI.

the addition of AFPII to the cryopreservation medium improves the protection against freezing of sea bream (Sparus aurata) spermatozoa, with respect to DMO or DMSO + AFPI, and that specific proteins of sperm flagella and head membranes can be used as markers related to procedures of fish spermatozoan cryopreservation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new and original application of antifreeze proteins in fish sperm cryoprotectant media.
the identification of proteins involved in the cryoprotective mechanism and the identification of new markers of the spermatozoa damage due to cryoprotectants.
the identification and characterization of proteins that are differentially expressed in cryopreserved spermatozoon and may be used as markers of the freezing-thaw process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AFPIII, with respect to DMPA or DMSO+AFPI, improves sperm quality after freezing-thawing.
AFPIII is a good additive to cryopreservation media, and the proteins identified here could represent good markers of the quality of sperm after cryopreservation.
AFPIII, in the cryopreservation procedure of sea bream, improves the protection against the freezing-thaw process respect to DMSOl or DMSO + AFPI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of antifreeze proteins to cryopreservation media can improve sperm quality and the addition of AFPIII is more effective than the addition of AFPl.
AFPIII, a fish antifreeze protein, is able to reduce the loss in sperm quality due to cryoprotection, and this is associated with a reduced number of changes in the protein profile of sperm flagella.
AFPIII can be considered an effective cryoprotective agent in fish sperm cryoprotection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cryopreserved spermatozoon quality can be improved by the addition of antifreeze proteins.
AFPIII is a promising cryoprotectant for sea bream cryopreserved spermatozooa.
the addition of AFPIII in the cryopreservation medium of sea bream improves sperm quality.
